principle: Source quality is evaluated for the claim being made. Identity, archaeology, survey response, theology, historical testimony, biomedical mechanism and supernatural report are different evidentiary objects.

tiers.A: Primary scholarly dataset, primary institutional text, official statistics or peer-reviewed source with explicit provenance
tiers.B: Curated scholarly/reference infrastructure suitable for identity, place, bibliography, archives or contextual metadata
tiers.C: Discovery/index source; candidate generation only until underlying source review
tiers.R: Reference media; visual context only unless separately bound to evidence
tiers.L: Licensed/restricted source; metadata may be represented but redistribution follows source terms

sources.name: Database of Religious History
sources.claim_policy: Expert coding remains attributed and scoped; mappings do not establish causation.

sources.name: Pulotu
sources.claim_policy: Comparative coding is not proof of diffusion or descent.

sources.name: D-PLACE
sources.claim_policy: Focal year and coded state remain observation metadata, not origin dates.

sources.name: Seshat Global History Databank
sources.claim_policy: Require variable-level citation, coding notes and versioned snapshot before analytical use.

sources.name: ARIADNE Research Infrastructure
sources.claim_policy: Discovery and material context do not establish symbolic interpretation by themselves.

sources.name: Pleiades
sources.claim_policy: Place reconciliation only; geographic association is not religious influence.

sources.name: World Historical Gazetteer
sources.claim_policy: Place links need temporal overlap before contact can be considered plausible.

sources.name: Crossref
sources.claim_policy: Bibliographic metadata is not evidence.

sources.name: OpenAlex
sources.claim_policy: Citation links measure scholarly relationships, not truth or evidentiary independence.

sources.name: PubMed / MEDLINE
sources.claim_policy: Underlying papers require review. Modern mechanisms never authorize retrospective diagnosis from narrative resemblance.

sources.name: Europe PMC / PMC
sources.claim_policy: Use only rights-compatible text; mechanistic findings remain population- and construct-scoped.

sources.name: World Values Survey
sources.claim_policy: Survey answers describe sampled populations under specific instruments and dates, not timeless religious properties.

sources.name: European Values Study
sources.claim_policy: Preserve survey wave, country, weights, questionnaire wording and missingness.

sources.name: Pew Research Center Religion datasets
sources.claim_policy: Preserve methodology and distinguish affiliation, practice, belief, switching and demographic estimates.

sources.name: Primary scriptures, inscriptions and institutional documents
sources.claim_policy: Text content is evidence that a text says something, not automatic evidence that every adherent believed or practiced it.

sources.name: HRAF / eHRAF
sources.claim_policy: Respect license; store locators and derived mappings only where redistribution is permitted.

sources.name: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum
sources.claim_policy: Use event- and community-specific records; never generalize victim or institutional behavior beyond evidence.

sources.name: The Holy See document archive
sources.claim_policy: Official texts establish institutional statements; reception and lived practice require separate evidence.

sources.name: Museum open-access/reference media
sources.claim_policy: Images remain reference context unless explicitly bound to a claim/evidence record.

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons reviewed media
sources.claim_policy: Identity and rights must be source-verified before render.
